schema.name: agent_name
schema.description: Observed agent, and part of the key rather than merely a column on it. Trajectory ids being unique across agents is an assumption about the observed agent's telemetry, which AQA does not control.

schema.name: trajectory_id
schema.description: The conversation this payload is of. With agent_name it is the whole key: no run_id, because the conversation is the same thing whichever sweep sampled it, and deduplicating the bulky copy across sweeps is the point of this table.

schema.name: created_at
schema.description: When this copy was stored. Partition column, and what the retention window expires on.

schema.name: status
schema.description: What this stored copy is: ingested (the whole conversation is here), partial (assembled from lossy telemetry -- something was missing), or truncated (nothing was wrong with the telemetry and we chose to cut it, because a turn exceeded the write cap). Not trajectories.ingest_status, which is one sweep's attempt rather than the copy.

schema.name: turn_count
schema.description: How many trajectory_payload_turns rows belong to this payload, so a reader can tell a short conversation from a partly-written one.

schema.name: agents
schema.description: AgentData.agents: the static config of each agent in the system -- system instructions, tool definitions. It belongs to the conversation rather than to any one turn, which is why this manifest is a table of its own beside the turns.

schema.name: agent_revision
schema.description: Deployment revision that served this conversation, as the telemetry reported it. Part of the evidence: an archived conversation outlives the telemetry it came from, and what an agent did is only judgeable against the build that did it. Null for a source that reports no revision, which denotes its single unnamed revision rather than an unknown one.
